title: PATCH /api/box/operator-config (409 | 422 | 403)
description: A REFUSED configuration mutation. Source: src/box/routes.ts. Refusals are always EXPLICIT and always NAMED — nothing is silently deferred and nothing is partially applied, so a client that receives this knows with certainty that the configuration is unchanged. `applied: false` is required and constant precisely so that property is impossible to misread. 409 means a stale `version` (another operator or tab changed the configuration first; re-read and retry). 422 means validation or policy refused the change, with one entry in `problems` per offending field. 403 means the operator's role is insufficient for a risk-increasing change. `version` is the CURRENT authoritative version, so a client can resynchronise without a second request. CLOSED so an added field is caught.

applied.description: Always false. A refusal never partially applies a patch, so this is a constant rather than a flag a reader has to interpret.

version.description: The CURRENT authoritative configuration version, so the client can resynchronise without a second round trip. On a 409 this is the version the client should have echoed.

problems.description: One entry per offending field. Non-empty: a refusal with no stated problem would be exactly the silent refusal this surface forbids. `key` is '__patch__' for problems concerning the request as a whole.
